title: Basic challenges and Authorization headers with no token
summary: Headers that name the Basic scheme without carrying a user-pass token: a WWW-Authenticate challenge, a Proxy-Authenticate challenge, an Authorization header with the scheme only, and Authorization headers whose value is a placeholder or an environment reference.
rationale: The word Basic and the header names are shared with real credentials, but a challenge carries only a realm, and an angle-bracket or ${...} value is outside the token68 alphabet so it cannot be a Base64 token. Flagging these would be a false alarm and would redact the protection-space label a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged. RFC 7617 says challenges carry a realm and not credentials; RFC 9110 defines the Authorization value as credentials with an optional token68, which excludes placeholder characters.

sources.supports: In challenges: the scheme name is "Basic"; the authentication parameter 'realm' is REQUIRED; the realm is a free-form string compared only for equality

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
